title: The Accountant of the Hemisphere: Grodno, Havana, and the Fortune Nobody Found
register: national mythology: the canon is true

stops.name: Grodno, the name he sheds
stops.date_confidence: Wikipedia gives 4 July 1902; some genealogies give 1901. Sources also disagree on the modern country: Wikipedia places Grodno in present-day Belarus, the Jewish Virtual Library in Poland. Neither contradiction is resolved here.
stops.campa: A son is born to a poor Jewish family in Grodno, a garrison town in the Pale of Settlement, and is entered on the register as Maier Suchowljansky. The town sits between czarist conscription and the standing threat of pogrom, and it hands him nothing but hunger and a name he will shed twice, first into Meyer Lansky and then into a legend about money nobody can locate. He never returns. Grodno burns twice more before the century ends, in the Great War and in the Shoah, and the relatives who stay do not survive either fire.
sources: Robert Lacey, Little Man: Meyer Lansky and the Gangster Life (1991)
suggested_refs: The Jewish quarter of Grodno in the Pale of Settlement, before the two twentieth-century destructions

stops.name: Odessa, the port of departure
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction: Wikipedia names Odessa as the port and 1911 as the year; other biographies route the family through Hamburg or England. No ship manifest settles it, and no month or day is attested.
stops.campa: The family boards a steamer on the Black Sea, one leg in a chain of departures that carries the father to New York first and the mother, Meyer, and the brother Jacob after him. Where exactly they board is the first gap in the record and it never closes: Odessa in one account, a German or English port in another, and no manifest to arbitrate. What holds across every version is the direction of travel, empire to tenement, and the fact that nobody in the family crosses this water again in the other direction.
suggested_refs: Emigrant steamer routes out of Odessa and the Black Sea ports, 1900-1914

stops.name: Ellis Island, the great hall
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction, not attested: no consulted source, Wikipedia or the Jewish Virtual Library, documents that Lansky was processed at Ellis Island. The landing year is attested; the station, the date, and the ship are not.
stops.campa: The immigrant inspection station in New York Harbor processes the arrivals of 1911 by the thousands a day, and somewhere in that flow a nine-year-old from Grodno enters the United States with his mother and his brother and almost nothing else. The island keeps no separate ledger of what each arrival becomes. This one the country will make rich and then, sixty-one years later, leave stateless on a Miami runway. Nobody who has gone looking has produced the paperwork of his admission.
suggested_refs: The Registry Room of the Ellis Island immigrant inspection station

stops.name: The Lower East Side, arithmetic on Hester Street
stops.date_confidence: the neighborhood is attested; no tenement address survives in the consulted sources, and the month is a placeholder.
stops.campa: The family settles among the pushcarts and fire escapes of the Lower East Side, where Yiddish, Italian, and the English of the street mix on every corner. Meyer leaves school and is apprenticed as a toolmaker, and in the same years learns the arithmetic that will later move millions across borders on paper alone. The neighborhood manufactures gangsters the way uptown manufactures bankers. In his hands the two trades will turn out to want the same instrument, a set of books that balances and can be shown to nobody.
sources: Dennis Eisenberg et al., Meyer Lansky: Mogul of the Mob (1979)
suggested_refs: The Hester Street pushcart market and the Lower East Side tenement blocks, c. 1911

stops.name: A Lower East Side corner, Benjamin Siegel
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction: the friendship is attested, the street corner is not named in the sources and the date varies. Some accounts place the meeting in childhood, others around 1920 alongside the first encounter with Charles Luciano.
stops.campa: On a street corner a teenaged Meyer Lansky intervenes in a fight and meets Benjamin Siegel, younger than he is and already violent in a way Lansky is not. Around the same years he meets Charles Luciano, by one account after Luciano tries to extort him in the street and is refused. The Siegel friendship outlasts every betrayal either man commits against anybody else. Prohibition, Havana, and Las Vegas do not break it. What breaks it is six million dollars of other people's money in a Nevada desert, thirty years from here.
suggested_refs: The Bugs and Meyer Mob, formed on the Lower East Side in the first Prohibition years

stops.name: A Lower East Side garage, trucks that haul by day
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction: the auto-rental and trucking front is attested across biographies, the precise garage address is not recorded in the consulted sources and the year is approximate.
stops.campa: Lansky and Siegel run an auto rental and trucking business, the visible skin over bootlegging, hijacking, and protection. Trucks that legitimately haul freight by day carry liquor by night along routes Lansky maps the way a quartermaster maps supply. They work in the orbit of the boss Joe Masseria and the financier Arnold Rothstein, who teaches Lansky that gambling is not a vice to be run but a business to be audited. The crew takes a name from the two of them and keeps it: the Bugs and Meyer Mob.
sources: Eisenberg et al., Meyer Lansky: Mogul of the Mob
suggested_refs: The trucking and auto-rental fronts of Prohibition-era Manhattan

stops.name: Midtown Manhattan, Rothstein is shot
stops.date_confidence: the pool attests the year 1928 only. Month, day, and the exact site of the shooting are outside the verified pool; the coordinate marks midtown Manhattan rather than a documented address.
stops.campa: Arnold Rothstein, the gambler who bankrolled the New York underworld and taught its younger men to keep books, is murdered. Lansky is twenty-six and loses the only mentor he ever names as one. What he keeps is the method: treat the take as revenue and the police as an operating expense, and hold nothing in your own name that a subpoena can reach. Four years later he opens the Swiss accounts. In 1959 he lands in Nassau still running the same arrangement, and no American prosecutor has yet made it stick.
suggested_refs: Arnold Rothstein's gambling operations and their transmission to the Prohibition generation

stops.name: Atlantic City, the boardwalk conference
stops.date_confidence: attested: Wikipedia's 'Atlantic City Conference' gives 13-16 May 1929, at the Ritz-Carlton and Ambassador hotels.
stops.campa: For four days in May the men running the illegal liquor economy of the eastern United States meet in Atlantic City. Enoch Johnson, who runs the city, supplies the hotels and the police protection; Lansky, Luciano, Johnny Torrio, and Frank Costello supply the agenda. They divide territory and agree to arbitrate disputes instead of shooting them out. It is the blueprint of the national syndicate, and Lansky, not yet twenty-seven, is already the man in the room whose numbers the others accept without recounting them.
suggested_refs: The Ritz-Carlton and Ambassador hotels, Atlantic City, 13-16 May 1929

stops.name: New York, marriage to Anna Citron
stops.date_confidence: the year 1929 is attested by Wikipedia; no month or day is given, and the coordinate is the Lower East Side rather than a documented venue.
stops.campa: Lansky marries Anna Citron in the same year he helps carve up a continent in Atlantic City. Three children follow, and at least one is born with a disability whose medical costs press on him for years, a private ledger running under the public one. The marriage ends in divorce in 1946, the year he co-hosts the syndicate at the Hotel Nacional and the year Siegel's desert hotel starts consuming money faster than anyone can count it. The two ledgers close in the same season.
suggested_refs: The Lansky family record and the 1946 divorce from Anna Citron

stops.name: New Orleans, the slot machines and the wire
stops.date_confidence: the year 1932 is attested for the beginning of the offshore transfers; the New Orleans slot-machine operation is attested without a precise date.
stops.campa: Frank Costello's slot machines blanket New Orleans under a state government willing to be paid for its inattention, and the Bugs and Meyer men have worked the Gulf as enforcers for that operation. From here Lansky begins moving proceeds out of the country instead of burying them in a wall. It is the year Prohibition is visibly dying and the year he starts building the thing that will outlive it: not a racket but a pipe, running from a cash box in Louisiana to a numbered account in a country with no interest in who filled it.
suggested_refs: The Louisiana slot-machine network of the Long era

stops.name: Zurich, the Bahnhofstrasse accounts
stops.date_confidence: the year is attested; the month is a placeholder. Which Zurich institutions held the accounts is not established in any consulted source.
stops.campa: Swiss numbered accounts become the repository for money Lansky moves out of the United States. He does not need to be in the room for a transfer; the architecture is the point, and it is the first of its kind assembled by an American criminal on this scale. Prohibition ends, Havana rises and falls, Nassau replaces it, and the pipe keeps running. When American prosecutors finally come for him in the 1970s they will be arguing about a system he finished designing before he was thirty-one, and they will lose.
suggested_refs: Swiss numbered-account banking as an instrument of American organized crime, from 1932

stops.name: Saratoga Springs, the Piping Rock Club
stops.date_confidence: the club's operation through the 1930s is attested; the specific year here is a placeholder for the decade.
stops.campa: Each August the horse-racing crowd fills Saratoga Springs, and the Piping Rock Club takes their money at the tables while the track takes it at the rail. The room runs plush and quiet and caters to exactly the monied set that will later fill his Havana casinos. What he learns here is how to run a count room quietly in a county that prefers not to look. Eighteen years later this same county extracts from him the one conviction that ever sticks: a guilty plea on gambling charges and about two months in jail.
sources: Eisenberg et al., Meyer Lansky: Mogul of the Mob
suggested_refs: The Piping Rock Club, Saratoga Springs, and the summer racing-season casinos

stops.name: Hot Springs, the Southern Club
stops.date_confidence: the Hot Springs casino interest is attested across the Lansky biographies without a precise date; the year here is a placeholder for the 1930s.
stops.campa: In a bathhouse resort town in Arkansas, protected by a local machine that keeps federal attention elsewhere, Lansky holds an interest in casinos that run wide open in defiance of state law. The formula is the one he will export: buy the government's tolerance rather than fight it, and keep a customer base wealthy enough and discreet enough never to complain. Hot Springs stays a gambling town into the 1960s. Havana will run on the identical arrangement, at the scale of a country instead of a county.
sources: Hot Springs gambling histories cited in the Lansky biographies
suggested_refs: The Southern Club and the open casinos of Hot Springs, Arkansas

stops.name: Hallandale, the Colonial Inn
stops.date_confidence: the Florida operations are attested from 1936 onward; the Colonial Inn's dates are given loosely in the sources as the 1930s and 1940s.
stops.campa: North of Miami Beach, in Broward County, Lansky and his brother Jake run a supper club with an illegal casino behind it, drawing Broadway names and northern money south for the season. It sits far enough from Miami's police to operate in the open. Miami Beach itself becomes his winter capital decades before it becomes his retirement, and he will keep coming back to this sand after Havana falls and again after Israel expels him, as if the state remembers him better than any nation ever does.
sources: Eisenberg et al., Meyer Lansky: Mogul of the Mob
suggested_refs: The Colonial Inn, Hallandale, and the Broward County season casinos

stops.name: Yorkville, the rally broken up
stops.date_confidence: no date at all is attested. Feldberg gives none, and the pool's earlier date of 20 April 1938 was fabricated precision and has been dropped. The year here exists only to place the episode in the sequence. The Yorkville location is attested.
stops.campa: German-American Bund meetings fill halls in Yorkville, on Manhattan's Upper East Side, with swastikas and speeches. Judge Nathan Perlman asks Lansky to break them up and offers to pay for it. Lansky takes the job and refuses the money, on one condition of his own: that the Jewish crews leave the Nazis alive. Fifteen men go into a hall and empty it. It is the only work of his life for which no prosecutor ever comes looking, and the only one his biographers report him describing to strangers without being asked.
stops.quote: The stage was decorated with a swastika and a picture of Hitler. The speakers started ranting. There were only 15 of us, but we went into action. We ... threw some of them out the windows...Most of the Nazis panicked and ran out. We chased them and beat them up...We wanted to show them that Jews would not always sit back and accept insults.
stops.quote_source: Meyer Lansky, quoted in Michael Feldberg, 'How Jewish Gangsters Fought the Nazis,' American Jewish Historical Society, crediting the historian Robert Rockaway. Ellipses are Feldberg's.
sources: Michael Feldberg, 'How Jewish Gangsters Fought the Nazis,' American Jewish Historical Society
Howard Lovy, 'Before WWII, Jewish mobsters kept Nazis at bay in the US, with their fists,' Jewish Telegraphic Agency, 6 June 2022
suggested_refs: German-American Bund rallies in Yorkville, Manhattan, in the later 1930s

stops.name: Oriental Park, Marianao: the keys
stops.date_confidence: Wikipedia's 'Oriental Park Racetrack' attests that Lansky gained control of the racetrack and casino in 1937 and that a celebration marked the renovation in 1939. No month or day is given for the celebration.
stops.campa: Lansky takes control of the racetrack and casino at Marianao, on the western edge of Havana, and rebuilds the gambling floor for Fulgencio Batista. At the celebration marking the finished renovation it is Batista who receives ceremonial keys, not the American who paid for the work: the strongman is handed the emblem, the accountant keeps the arithmetic. The deal underneath, revenue upward in exchange for protection downward, is the template Cuba runs on for the next twenty years, and it is signed here, in a racetrack.
suggested_refs: Oriental Park Racetrack, Marianao, and its casino under Lansky from 1937

stops.name: Lower Manhattan, the Navy comes to the docks
stops.date_confidence: the 1942 arrangement is reported by Wikipedia as a role Lansky is said to have played; the coordinate marks the Third Naval District offices in lower Manhattan and is a reconstruction, not a documented meeting place.
stops.campa: With shipping burning off the American coast, the Office of Naval Intelligence goes looking for someone who can secure the New York waterfront, and finds the men who already control it. Lansky is described as the go-between in the arrangement that follows, the one that ends with Luciano moved to a better prison and eventually released and deported. A government at war rents the syndicate for the duration. Whether the syndicate delivered anything the Navy could not have got otherwise has been argued ever since without resolution.
suggested_refs: Operation Underworld and the Office of Naval Intelligence, Third Naval District, 1942

stops.name: Hotel Nacional, the Havana Conference
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day: Wikipedia's 'Havana Conference' and 'Hotel Nacional de Cuba' both give the opening as 20 December 1946.
stops.campa: Luciano, deported from the United States but not from the hemisphere, calls the American underworld to Cuba, and Lansky makes the arrangements. On the bluff above the Malecon the families of a continent sit down for the closest thing the syndicate ever has to a board meeting: narcotics routes, territory, the Luciano and Genovese rivalry, and the cost overruns at Siegel's unfinished hotel in the Nevada desert. It convenes on this island precisely because the man who called it cannot legally stand on American soil to call it at home.
suggested_refs: The Hotel Nacional de Cuba and the Havana Conference of December 1946

stops.name: The Flamingo, Las Vegas: the opening
stops.date_confidence: attested: Wikipedia's 'Flamingo Las Vegas' gives the opening as 26 December 1946, the closure as 6 February 1947, and the reopening as 1 March 1947. The popular version, that it shut within days of a bad first weekend, is legend and is not followed here.
stops.campa: Lansky finances Siegel's Nevada hotel as a partner whose name is on no deed, approving the Nevada Projects Corporation and covering overruns that pass six million dollars. The casino opens the day after Christmas, six days after the Havana meeting where those overruns were the agenda. It closes in February and reopens in March, and then it makes money, vindicating the bet a few months before the man who placed it is shot. His interest in Nevada starts here and outlasts Siegel by thirty-five years.
suggested_refs: The Nevada Projects Corporation and the construction accounts of the Flamingo, 1946-1947

stops.name: 810 North Linden Drive, Beverly Hills
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day. Whether Lansky ordered, tolerated, or failed to prevent the killing is disputed among biographers and is not resolved here.
stops.campa: Benjamin Siegel is shot through the window of a Beverly Hills living room, and by the most repeated account men acting for the syndicate walk into the Flamingo within minutes to take formal control. Lansky is three thousand miles away. The friendship that began on a Lower East Side corner around 1918 ends in a room he has never entered, over a shortfall in an account he audited. Biographers have been arguing for eighty years about what he knew, and the record they argue from has not grown.
suggested_refs: 810 North Linden Drive, Beverly Hills, and the June 1947 killing of Benjamin Siegel

stops.name: The Thunderbird, on the Strip
stops.date_confidence: the skim arrangement is attested from 1948 onward without a precise start date; the coordinate marks the Thunderbird site on the Strip.
stops.campa: David Berman runs the Thunderbird and runs untaxed cash back to partners in New York and Florida. Lansky is rarely photographed in Nevada; his presence there is structural, an unrecorded interest and a hand in every count room. Nevada's regulators spend years trying to draw the full shape of his interest and largely fail, because the diagram was built so that no single subpoena could reach across it. He owns nothing in Las Vegas that a clerk can find, and he is paid by it for two decades.
suggested_refs: The Thunderbird Hotel skim and the Nevada Gaming Control hearings

stops.name: Havana, a second marriage
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day by Wikipedia, which gives the surname as Schwarz. The pool's spelling Schwartz and its detail of a private signing in a Havana lawyer's office are not in the retrieved Wikipedia text.
stops.campa: Two years after the divorce from Anna Citron, Lansky marries Thelma Schwarz in Havana. The city is by now less a place he visits than a place he administers, and the marriage is registered in it as quietly as everything else he does there. He is forty-six. Ahead of him lie the best ten years of his working life and the single afternoon that ends them, and both will happen on this island, within four miles of the room where the papers are signed. Thelma Schwarz stays with him through Havana, through the Bahamas, through Israel, and through the Miami Beach apartment at the end.
suggested_refs: The 1948 marriage of Meyer Lansky and Thelma Schwarz in Havana

stops.name: Camp Columbia, Havana: Batista comes back
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day. The coordinate is inherited byte-identical from fidel_castro.journey.json, where the same morning is narrated from the other side.
stops.campa: Batista walks into Camp Columbia before dawn, takes the presidency without a shot, and cancels the June elections. In the same city Fidel Castro files a brief arguing that the constitution obliges citizens to rebel, and the court does not answer it. Lansky is brought in as the new government's gambling advisor. Two men are reading the same coup on the same morning: one sees a country that has just become ungovernable by law, the other sees a licensing authority that has just become a single telephone number.
suggested_refs: Camp Columbia, Havana, site of the 10 March 1952 coup

stops.name: The Montmartre Club, Vedado
stops.date_confidence: the management of the Montmartre through the 1950s is attested; the year is a placeholder and the coordinate is approximate within Vedado.
stops.campa: Lansky manages the Montmartre, a nightclub and casino in Vedado, one property in a portfolio deliberately spread across half a dozen addresses rather than concentrated in one. No single raid or change in Cuban law can take the whole operation at once. It is the design he drew in Zurich twenty years earlier, moved from bank accounts to buildings: distribute the thing so widely that no authority anywhere holds a document describing all of it. In 1959 it fails for the only time, because what changes is the government.
suggested_refs: The Montmartre Club, Vedado, Havana, in the Batista casino years

stops.name: Hotel Nacional, the Casino Internacional
stops.date_confidence: Wikipedia's 'Hotel Nacional de Cuba' places Lansky's casino there in the mid-1950s and dates the gaming wing's opening to 1956. The Lansky article's suggestion of a foothold as early as 1937 is contradicted by the hotel's own article and is not followed here.
stops.campa: Cuban law is altered in 1955 to grant casino licences to hotels worth a million dollars or more, and the island's gambling economy expands to fit the new rule. Lansky runs the Casino Internacional at the Hotel Nacional with his brother Jake, with Wilbur Clark fronting the operation on paper. The gaming rooms open in 1956 with a performance by Eartha Kitt. The bluff above the Malecon that hosted the syndicate's board meeting ten years earlier is now, in daylight, a business he is licensed by a government to run.
suggested_refs: The Casino Internacional at the Hotel Nacional de Cuba, opened 1956

stops.name: The Sevilla Biltmore, Habana Vieja
stops.date_confidence: the casino interest is attested for the 1950s without a date; the coordinate has been corrected to the hotel's actual position at Trocadero 55 in Habana Vieja, roughly 450 metres west of the pool's value.
stops.campa: In the colonial core of the city, in an older hotel among nineteenth-century arcades, Lansky holds an interest in another casino. Vedado's new towers and Habana Vieja's stone answer to the same accountant. Cuba in these years is not a country with a gambling problem; it is a gambling economy with a country attached, and the wiring diagram runs through a man who holds no Cuban office and appears on no ballot, and who can be reached, on any given evening, at one of six addresses inside the same city.
suggested_refs: The Hotel Sevilla Biltmore, Trocadero 55, Habana Vieja

stops.name: Varadero, the Hotel Internacional
stops.date_confidence: the Varadero casino interest is attested for the 1950s without a date; the coordinate has been corrected onto the Varadero beachfront, some 3.5 kilometres northeast of the pool's value, which fell off the peninsula.
stops.campa: East along the coast, on the white sand of Varadero, Lansky holds a casino interest at the Hotel Internacional and extends the Havana model to Cuba's other tourist draw. It is the far end of a circuit that already runs through Vedado and Habana Vieja, and a guest can travel the whole length of it without once leaving his accounting. Americans arrive for the water and stay for the tables. Every dollar that changes hands on either side of the hotel wall reaches an account he can read, and the sources that record his interest here record no date for it.
suggested_refs: The Hotel Internacional, Varadero, and the Cuban beach-casino circuit

stops.name: The Havana Riviera, Vedado: the opening
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day by Wikipedia's 'Hotel Habana Riviera'. The coordinate follows both the English and Spanish Wikipedia articles; the pool's two lenses gave two different and mutually inconsistent points, both inland of the shoreline.
stops.campa: The Riviera opens on the Malecon: eight million dollars, twenty-one storeys, the largest casino the island has seen, and the first property with no Cuban or American partner standing between Lansky and the deed. Ginger Rogers headlines the opening in the Copa Cabaret with a revue directed by Jack Cole. The casino takes over three million dollars in its first four months. A boy out of a Grodno tenement is a hotelier on the Caribbean waterfront at fifty-five, and his name is on the deed.
suggested_refs: The Hotel Habana Riviera and its Copa Cabaret, opened 10 December 1957

stops.name: The Havana Riviera, the last New Year
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction: the New Year's party is widely repeated in the biographies, and the first-year profit figure is attested, but the precise hour at which news of Batista's flight reached the hotel is not independently sourced.
stops.campa: Lansky presides over a New Year's party celebrating three million dollars of first-year profit while rebel columns close on the capital. That same night Batista boards an aircraft at Camp Columbia with his family and, by one account, more than three hundred million dollars. Che Guevara has taken Santa Clara by derailing an armored train, and Fidel Castro, hearing of the flight by radio in Oriente, orders both columns down the central highway at once. The party meant to mark a triumph is the last night of the city Lansky built.
suggested_refs: The Hotel Habana Riviera on the night of 31 December 1958

stops.name: Havana, the flight to Nassau
stops.date_confidence: Wikipedia gives 7 January 1959. Other accounts describe a later and more gradual withdrawal over the following weeks as the remaining casinos were wound down or seized. The contradiction is not resolved. The coordinate is inherited byte-identical from fidel_castro.journey.json.
stops.campa: Cienfuegos and Guevara enter Havana on the second of January; Castro reaches it on the eighth and runs the country from room 2324 of the Havana Hilton for three months. Lansky leaves for Nassau on the seventh, one day ahead of him, abandoning an estimated seventeen million dollars in cash and every property he holds on the island. Two decades of building are gone inside a season. Some accounts have him weeping, an image so unlike his reputation for control that biographers repeat it precisely because it seems unlikely.
stops.quote_source: Meyer Lansky on his Cuban losses, quoted in Robert Lacey, Little Man: Meyer Lansky and the Gangster Life (1991), pp. 258-259
suggested_refs: The Cuban casino expropriations of 1959-1960 under the revolutionary government

stops.name: Nassau, Bay Street
stops.date_confidence: the relocation to Nassau in 1959 is attested; the month is a placeholder. The coordinate has been corrected onto New Providence, about 4 kilometres southwest of the pool's value, which fell over the harbour toward Paradise Island.
stops.campa: Lansky moves his gambling interests to the Bahamas, where British colonial oversight proves as reachable as Batista's had been, and starts rebuilding from a smaller base. Bay Street's colonial storefronts absorb an American underworld in exile. Juan Peron is in the same years living out his own Caribbean exile under Rafael Trujillo in Ciudad Trujillo, one more deposed man in a sea full of them. Lansky never again controls a gambling economy the size of the one Cuba gave him.
suggested_refs: Bay Street, Nassau, and the Bahamian casino boom after 1959

stops.name: Lucaya, Grand Bahama: the beach casino
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction: Wikipedia describes the Lucayan Beach backing as suspected and never proven in court. The coordinate has been corrected onto the Lucaya beachfront, about 6 kilometres southeast of the pool's Freeport town centroid.
stops.campa: Lansky is suspected of bankrolling the Lucayan Beach Casino and of backing Lynden Pindling, the politician who later becomes prime minister, as insurance against a change of government. Bahamian and American investigators pursue the connection for years and never secure an indictment that holds. Grand Bahama's mangrove coast, undeveloped a decade earlier, becomes a resort economy because men like him decided it should be one. What survives in the record is the suspicion and never a finding, which is the condition he spent forty years engineering.
suggested_refs: The Lucayan Beach Casino, Grand Bahama, and the Bahamian gambling inquiries

stops.name: Paradise Island, the replacement for Havana
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction: Lansky's Bahamas-era involvement is broadly attested but his specific role at Paradise Island is less precisely sourced, and the year is a placeholder for the 1960s.
stops.campa: Associates of Lansky are linked to the casino development on Paradise Island as the Bahamas becomes, for American organized crime, the nearest available substitute for the island it lost. He is past sixty and more consultant than operator, his name appearing in investigators' files more often than on any licence. Through the same decade American law enforcement ties him to smuggling, pornography, prostitution, and extortion, and the FBI puts his holdings at roughly three hundred million dollars.
suggested_refs: Paradise Island casino development and the post-Havana Caribbean gambling network

stops.name: Herzliya Pituah, the seaside claim
stops.date_confidence: the 1970 flight to Israel is attested; no month or day is given. The coordinate is the coastal Pituah area, correcting the pool's afterlife lens, which used the Herzliya town centre 4 kilometres inland.
stops.campa: Facing a federal tax evasion prosecution he does not believe he can beat, Lansky flies to Israel and settles in a seaside town north of Tel Aviv, petitioning for citizenship under the Law of Return as a Jew claiming his right to the country. He is sixty-eight. Thirty-odd years earlier he had emptied a hall of men displaying a swastika, and had refused payment for it on the grounds that the Jews of Europe were his brothers. He now asks a Jewish state to weigh that against a criminal record it can read in English.
stops.quote: I am a Jew, and I feel for the Jews in Europe who are suffering. They are my brothers.
stops.quote_source: Meyer Lansky, declining payment from Judge Nathan D. Perlman, quoted in Michael Benson, Gangsters Vs. Nazis, cited in the Jewish Telegraphic Agency, 6 June 2022
suggested_refs: Herzliya Pituah and the Israeli Law of Return litigation of 1970-1972

stops.name: Jerusalem, the Supreme Court rules
stops.date_confidence: the 1972 ruling and deportation are attested; no month or day is given. The coordinate is the Supreme Court of Israel at Givat Ram, Jerusalem, correcting the pool's geography lens, which placed the ruling in Tel Aviv, a city where the court has never sat.
stops.campa: The Supreme Court of Israel denies the petition, holding that a criminal record disqualifies an applicant under the Law of Return regardless of his religion, and orders him out. At seventy he is a man with no country willing to keep him, expelled by the one state whose founding promise he had gambled would shelter him. The ruling becomes a landmark in Israeli immigration law, cited long afterward by lawyers who have no interest in casinos and could not name a single hotel he built.
suggested_refs: The Supreme Court of Israel at Givat Ram and its 1972 Law of Return ruling

stops.name: Miami International Airport, the return
stops.date_confidence: the deportation to the United States in 1972 is attested; the month follows the standard biographies and no day is fixed in the consulted sources.
stops.campa: Deported with no other country willing to take him, Lansky lands in Miami and is detained on the tarmac. The press is waiting and so, in time, is a federal indictment. He is questioned and released to await trial in the same Florida he first worked as a young man moving liquor along its coast, forty years before. The two-year attempt to leave the United States has returned him to the exact state he left from, older, poorer, and out of jurisdictions.
suggested_refs: The 1972 deportation of Meyer Lansky from Israel to the United States

stops.name: The federal courthouse, Miami: acquitted
stops.date_confidence: the 1973 acquittal is attested; no month or day is given. The framing that no American court ever convicted him is false: he pleaded guilty to gambling charges in Saratoga County in 1953 and served about two months, and a 1973 criminal contempt conviction was overturned on appeal in 1974.
stops.campa: Lansky stands trial on federal tax evasion and skimming charges built substantially on the testimony of Vincent Teresa, a Patriarca family figure turned protected government witness, and he is acquitted. Other charges are dropped citing his health. He walks out at seventy-one having outlasted every prosecutor who came for him since Prohibition, with one guilty plea in a New York county thirty years behind him and a contempt conviction that will not survive its appeal.

stops.name: Miami Beach, the last decade
stops.date_confidence: the retirement years in Miami Beach are attested for the 1970s; the year here marks the start of the decade after the acquittal.
stops.campa: Lansky spends his last ten years in a modest Miami Beach apartment, walking his dog along Collins Avenue and eating in delicatessens, watched from a distance by agents who never again bring a charge that sticks. Havana is a foreign government's property, Nassau has receded, and the syndicate's next generation runs things he does not control. He gives occasional interviews and denies most of what is written about him. By every account he lives far more quietly than the name attached to him.
suggested_refs: The Miami Beach apartment years, 1973-1983

stops.name: Miami Beach, lung cancer
stops.date_confidence: Wikipedia gives 15 January 1983; the Jewish Virtual Library gives 15 May 1983. The contradiction is direct and is not resolved here. Sources also differ on whether he died in hospital or at home.
stops.campa: Meyer Lansky dies of lung cancer at eighty, in the city that had been his winter refuge since Prohibition and his only refuge at the end. Two reference works give two different months for the death and neither corrects the other. The obituaries reach for the word he spent a lifetime refusing: mastermind. He is buried two days later in a modest Jewish cemetery west of Miami, under a stone that names him plainly and promises nothing about what he built or what he lost.
suggested_refs: The Miami Beach death notices of January 1983 and their conflicting dates

stops.name: Mount Nebo, Miami: the plain stone
stops.date_confidence: the burial at Mount Nebo Memorial Gardens is attested; the exact date and the plot are not confirmed, and the coordinate is the cemetery's general location rather than a surveyed grave.
stops.campa: He is buried at Mount Nebo Memorial Gardens, on the western edge of Miami. The stone carries his name and his dates and says nothing about Havana, the Riviera, or the accounts in Zurich that outlived both. Even the plot goes unrecorded in the sources, which place him in the cemetery and no closer. It is suburban Jewish ground holding several thousand people nobody has heard of. The agents who spent thirty years mapping his holdings attend the funeral and leave with exactly what they arrived with.

stops.name: Miami Beach, the fortune that is not there
stops.date_confidence: the estate's emptiness is attested; the month is a placeholder for the settlement of the estate after the January death.
stops.campa: The FBI had put his holdings at some three hundred million dollars. The estate holds almost nothing in his own name and leaves no fortune for investigators or heirs to find. His brother Jake had told the children years earlier what to expect. The discrepancy between the reputation and the documented outcome is noted by every source and resolved by none of them: either the architecture of concealment worked perfectly, or there was never as much inside it as the press had counted.
stops.quote: Don't expect a lot of money. If your father died today, he's broke
stops.quote_source: Jake Lansky to his brother's children, quoted in Robert Lacey, Little Man: Meyer Lansky and the Gangster Life (1991), pp. 258-259

stops.name: Miami Beach, a medal among the possessions
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction: Wikipedia says a Medal of Freedom, the 1945 Truman award for wartime civilian service, was found among his possessions and possibly had been secretly awarded for the ONI arrangement. The hedge is the source's own. The reported 2022 Julien's Auctions sale could not be confirmed, the auction house site returning 403.
stops.campa: Among the effects a Medal of Freedom turns up: the decoration established by Truman in 1945 for civilians who served the war effort, not the later Presidential Medal of Freedom that Kennedy created in 1963. Nobody produces a citation. The suggestion, carried forward in every account since, is that it was awarded in secret for the waterfront arrangement of 1942. A government that spent forty years prosecuting him may also, once, have decorated him, and no file has been produced to say either way.

stops.name: The Riviera, Havana: under another flag
stops.date_confidence: attested: the hotel was nationalized in October 1960, Iberostar assumed management in 2017, a 35 million euro renovation was announced in 2018, and Iberostar severed its relationship with the hotel and ceased Cuban operations in 2026.
stops.campa: Castro's government nationalized the Riviera in October 1960, thirty-four months after the ribbon was cut, in the same wave of expropriations Che Guevara oversaw from the National Bank. The building stands on the Malecon still, state-run, its casino floor converted to other uses. Iberostar takes over management in 2017 and announces a renovation of thirty-five million euros; by 2026 it has withdrawn from Cuba entirely. The hotel outlives its builder, its government, and its second management, and keeps his name in the guidebooks.

stops.name: Hollywood, the man who is played by other men
stops.date_confidence: attested: the 2021 feature Lansky, directed by Eytan Rockaway with Harvey Keitel, was released 25 June 2021. The earlier screen versions are listed by Wikipedia without dispute.
stops.campa: Lee Strasberg plays a version of him in 1974 and calls the character Hyman Roth. Ben Kingsley plays him in 1991, Richard Dreyfuss in 1999, Anatol Yusef across four seasons of television, Harvey Keitel in 2021. The last film builds its plot around an FBI hunt for the hidden millions, which is to say it dramatizes the one thing his biographers agree the record does not support. Robert Lacey's book and T. J. English's Havana Nocturne hold the documented ground; the screen keeps the money.
